newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Makhteshim Q1 net up at $13.2 mln.
newsitem.headline: Makhteshim Q1 net up at $13.2 mln.

text.p: Makhteshim Chemical Works Ltd, a subsidiary of Koor Industries.
Note: The 1997 results include contributions from recent acquisitions made by Makhteshim.

The Israeli company, a maker of generic agrochemicals, said in a statement that most of the increase in 1997 sales was due to the contribution from these new subsidiaries. It said 1997 sales in dollar terms were eroded because of the strengthening of the U.S. currency.

The first quarter is the weakest for its South American subsidiaries, where the farming season (in the southern hemisphere) begins in the second half of the year, Makhteshim said. Sales and profit margins of these new subsidiaries are expected to increase in the second half, it said.

Managing director Shlomo Yonas said estimates for continued growth in the agrochemicals market in Brazil are strengthening as the Brazilian economy stabilises and the government frees up land for agriculture.
Makhteshim said it is continuing to develop new products, most of them targeted in the first stage at penetrating the South American market.
